description: We are Team Gravity, a group of innovative developers, designers, and problem-solvers driven by our interest in space exploration, science, and emerging technologies. We combine software development, 3D visualization, AI, and analytical thinking to transform complex space science and engineering challenges into interactive, engaging, and educational experiences.
summary:
GRAVITY is a free browser game where players design a real space mission from start to finish. They choose a scientific objective (Earth observation, a lunar orbiter or a Mars explorer), turn it into requirements, build a spacecraft in a 3D hangar, pick a launch vehicle and orbit, pass a readiness review, then fly the mission in 3D through four hands-on mini-games: launch steering, orbit insertion, science and downlink, and anomaly response.

Every choice has a consequence. Six live gauges (mass, power, budget, data, communications and time) show the trade-offs as they happen, and a deterministic simulation scores the result. The mission report explains why the mission succeeded or failed and compares the design with real NASA missions. "Analyse my design" and an auto-fix tool show players how to improve instead of only saying what is wrong.

Real missions are a balance, with no single perfect answer. GRAVITY teaches that systems-thinking to students and space fans through play, using margins and methods drawn from NASA mission-design guidance. It works offline, needs no account, and runs on phones.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

GRAVITY walks players through the same flow NASA mission teams follow, in six stages:

1. Objective: pick science goals, each weighted by importance.

2. Requirements: the game derives measurable requirements (resolution, coverage, data volume, power, link margin).

3. Spacecraft: build in an interactive 3D hangar (bus, instruments, power, propulsion, comms, thermal, computer). Every part has mass, power, cost and data trade-offs, and an X-ray view and a deployment test show how it fits together.

4. Launch & orbit: choose from 13 orbits around Earth, the Moon and Mars and from five launch-vehicle classes. Compatibility (payload capacity, delta-v, fairing) is checked automatically.

5. Readiness review: a checklist and a 5x5 risk matrix with mitigations. "Analyse my design" lists problems with plain-language fixes, and "Auto-fix my design" repairs the design step by step and explains each change.

6. Flight & report: a 3D flight with four playable mini-games (launch steering through Max-Q, an orbit-insertion burn, science targeting and downlink to ground stations, and anomaly response to events like solar storms or lost antenna lock), plus an optional autopilot at 1x/5x/20x speed. The report gives a mission score and a separate pilot score, explains why each requirement passed or failed ("because you chose..."), runs a what-if analysis showing which single change matters most, and matches the design to real NASA missions such as Landsat 9, LRO and MAVEN.

Three difficulty levels (Explorer, Engineer, Flight Director) change margin targets (10/20/35%), event rates and which advanced parts are unlocked. Ten kinds of random events make each flight different, while the same design and seed always give the same result. Designs can be saved, shared with a code and compared on a trade-space chart.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Players learn by consequence, not by quiz. Concepts like power margins, link budgets, delta-v and data rates are introduced exactly when they matter, with "Why does this matter?" explanations, a searchable glossary and hints on Explorer. Because several different designs can win each mission, players learn that engineering is about balance and trade-offs. GRAVITY is free, needs no login, collects no personal data, works offline as a Progressive Web App, runs on phones and laptops, and is built to WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility (keyboard play, screen-reader labels, reduced motion, no colour-only status), so classrooms can use it anywhere.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

TypeScript throughout, in a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo.

- Web: React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Zustand; 3D with three.js, React Three Fiber and Drei, using custom GLSL shaders for the planets, atmosphere, stars, engine plumes and the procedural spacecraft (no downloaded 3D models). The simulation runs in a Web Worker.

- Engine: a pure, deterministic TypeScript simulation and scoring engine (orbit periods from Kepler's law, rocket-equation delta-v, solar power from the NASA solar constant, link budgets, data volume, risk and margins), shared by the web app and the server.

- Data: all game numbers live in JSON catalogs validated with Zod; every value is labelled NASA, DERIVED or GAME, and a public data ledger records each source.

- Server (co-op mode, in progress): Node.js, Fastify, Socket.IO, PostgreSQL and Redis, with server-authoritative scoring.

- Quality: Vitest and fast-check tests (including balance tests proving every mission is winnable at every difficulty), axe accessibility tests, ESLint, Prettier, GitHub Actions CI and CodeQL. Hosted on Vercel.

CREATIVITY

GRAVITY combines a strategy design game with action mini-games, so the spacecraft you design is the one you fly: a weak antenna makes downlink harder, too little propellant makes the insertion burn fail. The report doesn't just grade you; it tells the story of why the mission turned out the way it did and links it to real missions.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty (game values are clearly labelled and never presented as NASA data), a young audience (no chat, no personal data, plain language), accessibility, offline and low-end-device support, deterministic and testable game balance, and keeping the game fun without oversimplifying the trade-offs.
